project_metadata.job_description:
I have my own brand for male enhancement product which we promote on Social Media. We need video ads for the same product. 

I have attached a sample video which was created by me but i need better video quality. 

Only those must apply who think they can bring sales through their video. They must have deep knowledge about the category we are working in specifically indian market. Video needs to be created in Hindi.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I completed a frame-by-frame review and audio analysis of all three. These are my findings.

Before anything else, there is an important point to understand: the two creatives you consider successful are actually the same video.

newvid.mp4 is 1080x1080 at 3.1 Mbps, while Purushveda\_Herbs is 720x720 at 550 kbps. Their scene cuts occur on the exact same frames, both have an audio mean volume of 17.3 dB and a peak of 1.0 dB, and both contain the same silence points at 23.2s and 29.2s. The second file is merely Meta's compressed download of the first one after it was published.

This means you do not have two winning videos and one losing video. You have one winner and one loser. Because your winning pattern comes from a sample of one, diagnosing the third creative externally is difficult.

Here is why the third one failed.

1\. Rather than functioning as a video, it is essentially a static image accompanied by subtitles.

The winning creative contains 14 scene cuts over 30 seconds, with an average shot duration of 2.1 seconds, and the first cut occurs at 2.0 seconds.

By comparison, the unsuccessful creative has 1 cut during its 32.6 seconds. One image remains on screen throughout the first 21.8 seconds, followed by a single cut to a static product card that stays visible for the final 11 seconds.

Movement is what maintains the viewer’s attention. Meta evaluates the 3 second view, and the successful ad cuts at 2.0 seconds, just before that threshold. In the failed creative, viewers have nothing new to watch at second 2, second 5, or second 15. It provides neither a reason to stop scrolling nor anything that holds attention afterward.

2\. Its audio is 9 dB quieter, with eight separate stalls.

Winner: mean volume 17.3 dB, peak 1.0 dB, and two pauses over 30 seconds.
Failing: mean volume 26.2 dB, peak 9.0 dB, and eight silence gaps over 32.6 seconds.

The voice is identical in both, so the issue lies in editing and mixing rather than the voice itself. On a phone, a 9 dB difference is approximately half the perceived loudness. Additionally, the failed creative becomes silent eight different times without any underlying music bed, making it sound both quiet and hesitant.

3\. The opening presents the result rather than establishing the problem.

Its first frame immediately shows the positive outcome promised by the product. With no tension or curiosity gap, viewers have no incentive to continue. The successful creative starts with a situation instead of revealing the conclusion.

There is also a fourth problem shared by all three: each is formatted as 1:1 square. This completely sacrifices Reels and Stories placements and wastes vertical feed space. The next creative should therefore be delivered primarily in 9:16, with 4:5 as the secondary format.

Regarding what I would produce:

I would not make only one video. I would develop three separate angles using the structural principles already validated by your winner, with each supplied in 9:16 and 4:5. That gives you genuine material to test instead of relying on a single creative and hoping it succeeds. Individual creatives do not reliably create winners; tested angles do.

Regarding your 50 INR CPL goal, I want to be direct because honesty is more useful than simply agreeing. Creative affects hook rate, hold rate, and CTR, but CPL is jointly determined by the creative, offer, landing page, and bidding. Anyone promising a specific CPL based only on a video is making a guess. What I can commit to is outperforming your current winner’s hook rate and hold rate, with the supporting numbers shown to you.

For accurate targeting, please send the winning creative’s hook rate, hold rate, link CTR, and landing page conversion rate. Those figures will reveal where your actual ceiling is.

messages.text:
I reviewed the data, and several points are immediately noticeable.

Your cost per lead is currently ₹76.52 compared with the ₹50 target, which puts the account 53% above its goal. However, the detailed metrics indicate that creative is not the sole issue.

The link CTR is 3.54%, which is genuinely strong and shows that the advertisement is attracting attention successfully. The main loss occurs after the click: just 59.7% of link clicks are being recorded as landing page views. In other words, approximately 40% of the clicks you pay for disappear before the page finishes loading or tracking them. That points to page speed or tracking configuration, not the video, and changing the creative cannot solve it.

More significantly, the Quality Ranking is Below Average, in the bottom 35%, even though both Engagement Rate and Conversion Rate are Above Average. This combination commonly indicates that the ad or landing page experience is generating negative signals, such as hidden ads or reports, despite users who click converting well. If it remains unresolved, it will quietly raise CPMs throughout the account regardless of the quality of the next creative.

Therefore, to genuinely reach a ₹50 CPL rather than merely produce a better video, I would prioritize the following:

1\. Build a new creative around the structural principles validated by the winner, including quicker cuts, corrected audio levels, a proper hook, and delivery in 9:16 and 4:5.
2\. Review landing page loading speed and the pixel/tracking configuration, because the 40% drop-off is consuming budget independently of the advertisement. If helpful, I can inspect this directly; identifying tracking and funnel problems like this is part of the automation side of my work, not only video production.
3\. Track the Quality Ranking after corrections are made, since that metric will show whether the negative-feedback problem is being resolved.

If you agree with this approach, I can prepare a quotation and timeline for rebuilding the creative. I can also include a note about the landing page correction if you want me to handle that as well. Let me know, and I’ll send everything over.
